subject.title: fix: failed cloud dispatch leaks the session's managed worktree

question: Should deleting a session-owned worktree always remove its checkout after creating a snapshot, replacing the previous behavior that preserved dirty or unpushed checkouts at their original path?
rationale: This is an intentional recovery and data-retention policy change, not merely a mechanical cleanup fix; source and user-facing restoration proof are needed to confirm the snapshot is an adequate replacement for a preserved checkout.

options.title: Adopt snapshot-and-remove
options.body: Accept the new ownership model after proving that committed and local-edit recovery from the snapshot is accessible to an operator.

options.title: Preserve dirty checkouts
options.body: Retain the current lossless-only deletion behavior and fix the orphaning path with a narrower cleanup or ownership handoff.

recommendation.title: Adopt snapshot-and-remove
recommendation.body: Accept the new ownership model after proving that committed and local-edit recovery from the snapshot is accessible to an operator.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context identifies this person as the author of both the reproduction and the proposed worktree-lifecycle policy change.
